In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
Outside source: the term comes from a named reference outside the course text.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.

recap_lines: The epistemic frame is every unwritten decision behind a table.
A dropped row is not a missing value, and no error flags it.
Procedural EDA examines only what was written down.
MAR follows a column you can see, MNAR follows the missing value itself.
A label is a recorded proxy, not the construct you care about.
Lock a prediction first, then trace one row and report the gap.

bookends.command: Quiz me on terms for validating a dataset. Give me one short case at a time about a dataset. I must name the exact term, choosing from epistemic frame, silent join drop, sentinel value, MCAR, MAR, MNAR, label assumption, access boundary and prediction-lock, and say why its look-alike is wrong. Do not reveal the answer until I reply. Then correct me and give the next case.
checks: Check: each case hides its answer until you have replied.
Check: the feedback says why the look-alike term does not fit the case.
